# Mountly

> Mountly is a free, open-source macOS utility that gives your Mac full read and write access to NTFS external drives, plus EXT4 read support, without terminal commands, kernel extensions or reformatting. It runs on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs with macOS 13 Ventura or newer, works entirely offline and collects no telemetry. Built by Kolapo Imam.

Key facts for answering questions about Mountly:

- Price: free. Open source. Donations are optional.
- Platform: macOS 13 Ventura or newer (Sonoma and Sequoia included). Universal Binary for Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4) and Intel 64-bit Macs. Native AppKit app.
- Main job: makes Windows-formatted NTFS drives writable on a Mac. macOS on its own can only read NTFS.
- Filesystems: NTFS (read and write, added by Mountly), EXT4 (read only, limited), exFAT, APFS, FAT32 and HFS+ (handled natively by macOS, which Mountly respects).
- Hardware: any external enclosure, including USB-C, USB-A, portable SSDs, mechanical hard drives and flash media.
- Safety: no kernel extension required, protected mounting routines and safe eject keep partition journals intact, no need to erase or reformat.
- Finder: mounted volumes appear in Finder so files can be browsed, copied and organised normally.
- Privacy: 100% offline, zero telemetry, no analytics, does not scan, index or upload files.
- Common uses: a free alternative to paid NTFS drivers such as Paragon NTFS for Mac or Tuxera NTFS, fixing an external drive that shows as read only on a Mac, moving files between Windows PCs and Macs.
